key_insight: Dreaming Learning mitigates model collapse by training on high-temperature self-generated samples that counteract the loss of diversity caused by low-temperature sampling.
engineering_relevance: For generative models trained recursively on synthetic data, an auxiliary dreaming loss may help preserve diversity when data accumulation alone does not stop collapse.
method: Track collapse through the eigenvalue spectrum of a learned Markov transition operator.
Add an auxiliary loss on model-generated samples drawn at dreaming temperature T_d > 1.
Counter low-temperature sharpening to keep transition probabilities from vanishing and eigenvalues away from the unit circle.
evidence_signal: Spectral measurements over 5,000 generations support the mechanism, with mitigation also observed in LSTM language models and a 124M-parameter GPT-2.
watch_item: The spectral mechanism is studied in a controlled Markov setting; effectiveness and temperature tuning require validation for larger models and deployment data.
paper_title: Mitigating Model Collapse through Dreaming Learning
